In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8278): >## What this PR does / why we need it: >## Summary >- Add per-node kubelet health predicates (`MemoryPressure=False`, > `DiskPressure=False`, `PIDPressure=False`) to the autorepair test's > `WaitForReadyNodesByNodePool` call, ensuring the replacement node is > fully healthy before proceeding >- Add `WithInterval(15s)` to `validateNodePoolConditions` to reduce > API server polling and eliminate client rate limiter errors > >## Problem >- The `TestNodePoolAutoRepair` e2e test flakes when a replacement node >comes up `NodeReady=True` but with kubelet pressure conditions. CAPI >sets `MachineNodeHealthyCondition=False` (`NodeConditionsFailed`), >which propagates to `AllNodesHealthy=False` on the NodePool. >`validateNodePoolConditions` then times out after 20 minutes. > >- Additionally, `validateNodePoolConditions` polls every 3s (default), >generating ~400 API GETs over 20 min, triggering client rate limiter >errors. > >## Root cause >- `WaitForReadyNodesByNodePool` only verified `NodeReady=True` and did >not check kubelet health conditions. The test passed at ~7 min with an >unhealthy node, leaving `validateNodePoolConditions` to discover the >problem with insufficient time for the node to stabilize. > >## Design decisions >- **Reused `ConditionPredicate`/`WithPredicates`** instead of custom > helpers — the framework already logs predicate failures, giving > specific diagnostics (e.g., `wanted MemoryPressure=False, got True`) >- **Kept original collection predicates unchanged** — the built-in > count predicate in `WaitForNReadyNodesWithOptions` already ensures > the old node is fully removed >- **15s polling interval** matches the pattern in > `WaitForNodePoolConfigUpdateComplete` (15-20s with explicit comments > about rate limiting) >- **No stabilization window (`Consistently`)** — `validateNodePoolConditions` > already serves as a 20-min post-`Run()` stabilization check >- **No direct Machine condition check** — would require management > client access in the test interface; node-level pressure checks are > functionally equivalent to what CAPI evaluates >## Which issue(s) this PR fixes: > >Fixes [OCPBUGS-79471](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-79471) > >## Special notes for your reviewer: > >## Checklist: >- [x] Subject and description added to both, commit and PR. >- [x] Relevant issues have been referenced. >- [ ] This change includes docs. >- [ ] This change includes unit tests. Let me produce the final report. # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced - **Build ID**: 2046522614028963840 - **Target**: e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced - **PR**: #8278 (OCPBUGS-79471: fix(test): reduce e2e autorepair flakes from unhealthy node conditions) - **Failed Tests**: TestCreateCluster/ValidateHostedCluster, TestAutoscaling/ValidateHostedCluster ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` Failed to wait for 2 nodes to become ready in 45m0s: context deadline exceeded observed **v1.Node collection invalid: expected 2 nodes, got 0 DataVolume create-cluster-4hkq7-5kq6r-5fm5x-rhcos is not ready; Phase: Pending target PVC Pending and Waiting for a volume to be created either by the external provisioner 'openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com' or manually by the system administrator. ``` ### Summary Both TestCreateCluster and TestAutoscaling failed because zero KubeVirt worker nodes joined the hosted clusters within the 45-minute timeout. The root cause is an ODF/Ceph storage infrastructure issue: the DataVolumes backing the KubeVirt VM root disks were stuck in `Pending` phase for the entire test duration because the Ceph RBD CSI provisioner (`openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com`) never created the underlying PersistentVolumes. Without root disks, the VirtualMachines could not start, so no worker nodes ever registered. This failure is **unrelated to the PR changes**, which only modify autorepair test node-health predicates and polling intervals.
Root Cause The failure chain is: 1. **ODF/Ceph CSI provisioner unresponsive** — The `openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com` CSI provisioner did not create PVs for the DataVolume PVCs, despite the StorageCluster reporting as deployed and the `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd` storage class being present and set as default. 2. **DataVolumes stuck in Pending** — Both DataVolumes (`create-cluster-4hkq7-5kq6r-5fm5x-rhcos` and `create-cluster-4hkq7-5kq6r-lzxbt-rhcos`) were created at `11:34:56Z` and immediately entered `Pending` phase with the condition: _"target PVC Pending and Waiting for a volume to be created either by the external provisioner 'openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com'"_. They remained in this state for the entire 45-minute test window. 3. **KubeVirt VMs could not start** — Since the DataVolumes provide the RHCOS root disk image for each VM, the VirtualMachines could not boot. The KubeVirtMachine resources reported `DVPending` and `VMProvisioned=False`. 4. **No worker nodes registered** — Without running VMs, no kubelet could start, so zero nodes joined the hosted cluster's API server. The test waited 45 minutes for nodes and timed out. 5. **Hosted cluster incomplete** — With no worker nodes, cluster operators requiring node-level components (console, dns, image-registry, ingress, monitoring, network, etc.) could not become available, leaving `ClusterVersionAvailable=False` and `ClusterVersionSucceeding=False`. The same pattern affected both TestCreateCluster (expected 2 nodes, got 0) and TestAutoscaling (expected 1 node, got 0) identically, confirming the problem is infrastructure-wide rather than test-specific. **PR #8278 is not the cause.** The PR only modifies `test/e2e/nodepool_autorepair_test.go` (adding kubelet pressure condition checks to `WaitForReadyNodesByNodePool`) and `test/e2e/nodepool_test.go` (adding `WithInterval(15s)` to reduce polling). Neither file affects KubeVirt VM creation, DataVolume provisioning, or storage configuration. The TestCreateCluster and TestAutoscaling tests do not use the modified autorepair predicates.
Recommendations 1. **Retry the job** — This is an infrastructure flake caused by the ODF/Ceph storage backend not provisioning volumes. The PR changes are unrelated. 2. **If retry fails again**, investigate the Ceph cluster health on the management cluster: - Check if the `csi-rbdplugin-provisioner` pods in `openshift-storage` namespace are running and not crash-looping - Check the Ceph cluster health status (`ceph -s`) via the rook-ceph-tools pod - Review events in the `openshift-storage` namespace for Ceph OSD or MON errors 3. **Consider filing an ODF infrastructure bug** if this pattern recurs across multiple unrelated PRs, as it indicates a systemic issue with the Ceph RBD provisioner in the CI environment.
